creativeDirection: Night location photography: rebuild the corner-shop street as a real urban scene after dark, using the shopfront as the lead place and letting the other sleeves appear as small physical details within one clean, plausible photograph.
scene: A quiet city corner at night outside an old corner shop with big display windows and a tiled pavement, seen from eye level at the curb so the storefront fills most of the frame and the sidewalk slips away to the left. The street is empty except for a small dog sitting near the right foreground under the shop window, with painted and incidental details tying the other covers into the same block.

elements.element: the corner-shop street location with large windows, tiled sidewalk, neighboring buildings, and strong black-and-white architectural contrast translated into a real night scene
a small black-and-white dog seated at the lower right by the curb, with traces of dirty snow and icy slush along the edge of the pavement
a black outlined shooting star with trailing curved lines painted on the shop's side wall
a pale lavender tangle of fine looping lines and specks drifting across one window display as painted decoration or condensation drawing
a tiny bouquet of white daisy-like flowers tucked discreetly above the shop doorframe
brick, grayscale, and muted red accents in the neighboring facade

prompt: A quiet urban street corner at night, viewed from eye level near the curb in a 16:9 frame, focused on an old corner shop with large display windows and a tiled sidewalk receding left; the primary subject is a small black-and-white dog from reference image 2 sitting at the lower right by the curb under the glow of the shop window, with dirty snow and icy slush gathered along the pavement edge and no other people anywhere in the scene; rebuild the corner-shop place from reference image 1 as the main location with neighboring buildings, deep shadow, strong storefront geometry, and a grayscale city feel, add a black outlined shooting star with trailing curved lines painted on the shop's side wall from reference image 4, a pale lavender cloud of fine tangled looping lines and specks across one window display from reference image 5, and a tiny bouquet of white daisy-like flowers tucked above the shop doorframe from reference image 6, while reference image 3 contributes only muted brick, grayscale, and small red accent tones in the adjacent facade; photographic realism, night location photography, crisp editorial detail, clean surfaces, no haze or rain; off-centre environmental composition with the dog in the right foreground and the storefront dominating the middle ground, faces not applicable, sharp focus throughout, well-lit by warm shop windows and a cool streetlamp so every detail reads clearly at small size; palette of black, white, gray, olive green, muted red, lavender, and cream, with a quiet wintry mood. Nobody from reference images 1, 3 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The image contains no people at all: no figures, faces, hands, limbs, silhouettes, reflections, or shadows of people, in the foreground or the background.
